newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso closes firm on bourse, tax payments.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso closes firm on bourse, tax payments.

text.p: The peso closed firmer on Friday as foreign investors stepped into the bourse in late trade and local dealers selling dollars to meet tax bills, traders said.
"The peso gained ground due to a sharp gain on the bourse and dollars dumped by corporations," one trader said.
The benchmark 48-hour peso and its 24-hour stablemate closed 2.8 and 1.9 centavos firmer, respectively, at 7.8020/7.8080 and 7.7950/7.8050 per dollar.
"The system is awash with dollars," another trader said. "And dealers are dumping them."
Mexico's blue chip IPC index was up 1.09 percent at 3,742.17 percent when the foreign exchange market closed.
Traders noted several local corporations sold surplus dollars to meet Friday's deadline for peso-denominated tax bills.
Dollars also flowed into the local money market, traders said, so as to earn interest while U.S. stock markets are closed on Monday, Jan 20, for Martin Luther King Jr. Day.
There will be no same-day trading on Monday.
Same-day peso contracts had closed earlier 0.2 of a centavo weaker at 7.8110/7.8140 per dollar.
The 48-hour peso closed 2.6 centavos firmer than the close of trade last week, and 8.7 centavos stronger than at the end of last month. ((--Alexis Quiones, Mexico City newsroom
